source_user: Advanced cluster case GDR-117: Design a validation plan for GPUDirect RDMA between GPUs and NICs. Variant 117 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: verify topology and peer access, registration and pinning, IOMMU/container permissions, NIC-GPU affinity, direct versus staged copies, and compare bandwidth and CPU utilization. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Assume an authorized, isolated benchmark allocation and an otherwise unchanged distributed-training environment; platform and software details are unknown until measured. For corpus-05367 (117), first capture GPU/NIC models, PCIe/NVLink and NUMA topology, NIC-GPU affinity, link state, driver/firmware/runtime/container versions, peer-access capability, IOMMU and container permissions, buffer placement, registration and pinning behavior, process affinity, message sizes, concurrency, clocks, thermals, and test duration. Separate measured facts from estimates and do not change production settings during diagnosis.

Falsifiable hypothesis: with placement, clocks, concurrency, message sizes, and duration matched, a verified direct GPUDirect RDMA path will improve steady-state bandwidth (GB/s) and/or reduce host CPU utilization versus a host-staged control, without increasing p50/p95/p99 latency, timeout/retry/error rates, or data-integrity failures beyond predeclared limits. Verify the path using independent telemetry and a staged-copy control; do not infer direct transfer from throughput alone. Measure registration/setup separately from transfer, report transfer latency in microseconds, bandwidth in GB/s, CPU utilization as percent, and error/retry counts with denominators over repeated trials. Include warm-up, randomized or alternating order, identical payloads, checksums, and confidence intervals or trial dispersion.

Failure/rollback: stop and restore the prior configuration if correctness checks fail, errors/timeouts rise, thermals or link health leave safe limits, or the direct path cannot be proven. Record the exact failed prerequisite (topology, peer access, registration/pinning, IOMMU/container permission, affinity, or fallback), retain logs and versions, and require domain-owner authorization before any remediation. Evidence required before claiming improvement: topology and permission artifacts, direct-path counters/traces, matched baseline data, workload and unit definitions, repeated measurements, and integrity/rollback results.

source_user: Advanced cluster case GDS-1: Evaluate GPUDirect Storage for checkpoint and dataset I/O in distributed training. Variant 1 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate storage throughput from GPU DMA, validate filesystem and kernel support, measure queue depth and tail latency, compare CPU-staged I/O, and test restart consistency after interruption. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Assume an authorized, isolated test allocation with platform details to be established rather than guessed. For corpus-05376 (1), define the data path and checkpoint or dataset workload before tuning: GPU/NIC/storage topology and NUMA placement, filesystem and kernel/runtime/driver versions, container permissions, buffer placement, process and I/O affinity, file/object layout, request size, queue depth, concurrency, caching state, clocks, thermals, and duration. Distinguish storage throughput from GPU DMA and from end-to-end training impact.

Falsifiable hypothesis: after filesystem support and the GPUDirect Storage path are independently verified, matched workload size, cache state, queue depth, concurrency, and placement will increase sustained useful throughput (GB/s) and/or reduce host CPU utilization or training I/O stall time versus CPU-staged I/O, without unacceptable p50/p95/p99 latency, data-integrity errors, or restart inconsistency. Measure storage and GPU-DMA stages separately, report throughput in GB/s, latency in milliseconds, queue depth, CPU utilization, and error counts with denominators over repeated trials; use alternating controls, warm-up, checksums, and confidence intervals or dispersion.

Failure/rollback: stop and revert to the known-good CPU-staged path if support, permissions, direct-path evidence, checksums, checkpoint atomicity, restart consistency, thermal/link health, or error thresholds fail. Preserve logs and version/configuration artifacts, avoid destructive filesystem changes, and require owner authorization for remediation. Evidence required before claiming improvement: topology and support checks, direct-path telemetry, matched baseline results, workload/cache definitions, tail-latency and queue-depth data, integrity/restart tests, and explicit rollback results.
